title: What If the Biggest Hailstone Ever Found Fell Near You?

scenes.text: What if a hailstone as wide as a bowling ball fell? One really did.
On July 23, 2010, a storm over Vivian, South Dakota dropped a stone eight inches wide.
It weighed 1.94 pounds, a United States record, and the finder said it had been three inches wider before it started melting.
Stones grow in storms with updrafts estimated at 160 to 180 miles an hour, which hold them aloft.
The old size record was seven inches, set in Aurora, Nebraska, in 2003.
So a hailstone like this isn't a freak of the sky. It's a storm cloud that built something heavy.
